meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to access'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'accédé').

examples.text: Avec Mathias, c'est difficile d'accéder aux profondeurs.
examples.trans: With Mathias, it is difficult to reach the depths.

meanings.note: aller + infinitive: tu vas l'agacer = you're going to annoy her
Je vais déjeuner. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to go'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'allé').
Imperative used to encourage. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to go'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'allé').

examples.trans: I'm going to have lunch twice.

meanings.note: j'en ai assez = I've had enough, I'm fed up
Assez bien. Invariable French adverb meaning 'enough'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Il y a un macaron sur la table.

meanings.en: il y a = there is / there are

meanings.note: À bientôt = see you soon. Invariable French adverb meaning 'soon'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
determiner: ce soir = tonight, cette semaine = this week
pronoun: c'est = it is; tout ce que = all that

examples.text: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
Cette agence ne représente que des stars.

meanings.note: no preposition: chercher du travail

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to look for'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'cherché').

examples.text: J'ai un petit loft. Et je cherche du boulot.

Demander quelque chose à quelqu'un. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to ask'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'demandé').

examples.text: Si vous avez besoin d'aide, demandez.
examples.trans: If you need help, just ask.

meanings.note: Dévorer un livre. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to devour'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'dévoré').

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'sometimes'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'maybe'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
